cards.text: We're in Egypt now, friend. The people of Judah went down there even though the LORD told them to stay home (Jeremiah 43:4-7), and they've spread out to Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis and Pathros. Then the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah the prophet about every one of them.
The LORD of Hosts opens with something they've all seen with their own eyes. Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, lying in ruins today. No slideshow needed. They just LEFT it.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say Jerusalem and the cities of Judah are lying in ruins?

answers.text: Because of the evil they had done
Because their walls were built too weak
Because their army was far too small

cards.question: The LORD says the other gods Judah burned incense to were gods their fathers had always known.

cards.text: And God didn't spring this on anybody. He sent His servants the prophets again and again: 'Do not do this detestable thing that I hate.' That's an alarm clock going off, and somebody hitting snooze. Over. And over. And OVER.

cards.question: When the prophets kept warning them, the people of Judah turned from their wickedness and stopped burning incense to other gods.
So the LORD's wrath and anger poured out and ___ in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem.

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to the people right there in Egypt with a question. Why are they doing such great harm to themselves, cutting off man and woman, child and infant from Judah, until there's no remnant left?

cards.question: Now that they live in Egypt, what are the people of Judah doing that provokes the LORD to anger?

answers.text: Selling their own people as slaves

cards.text: Then God asks them straight out: have they forgotten? The wickedness of their fathers, of the kings of Judah and their wives, and their OWN wickedness back in the streets of Jerusalem.

cards.question: The LORD says that to this day the people have humbled themselves and followed His instruction.

cards.text: So the LORD says He has set His face to bring disaster and cut off all Judah. And the remnant who decided to move to Egypt? New zip code. Same God watching.

cards.question: From the least to the greatest, how does the LORD say the remnant who went to Egypt will die?
The LORD says He will punish those living in Egypt just as He punished Jerusalem.

cards.text: Here's the part that stings. These people long to go back to Judah and live there again.

cards.question: Who does the LORD say will make it back from Egypt to Judah?

cards.text: Now the people answer Jeremiah. And this isn't two guys grumbling in the back row. It's a GREAT assembly: the men who knew their wives were burning incense to other gods, the women standing by, and the people living in Egypt and Pathros.

cards.question: What does the great assembly tell Jeremiah about the word he spoke in the name of the LORD?

answers.text: We will not listen to you
We will do all you say

cards.text: Then they say what they WILL do. They vowed to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just like their fathers, their kings and their officials did back in Judah. Wrong direction. Full commitment.

cards.question: Back when they burned incense to the Queen of Heaven in Judah, what do the people say life was like?

answers.text: Plenty of food and no disaster
Long years of drought and plague

cards.question: The people say that since they stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven, they have lacked everything.

cards.text: So their read is: life fell apart when we STOPPED. Friend, that's like maxing out a credit card, cutting it up, and when the bills show up... deciding the scissors were the problem.
Then the women speak up. They made sacrificial cakes in her image and poured out drink offerings to her, and they ask Jeremiah a question about their husbands.

cards.question: The women say they burned incense to the Queen of Heaven without their husbands knowing.

cards.text: Now Jeremiah answers all of them, men and women. He brings up all that incense burned in Judah's cities and Jerusalem's streets, by them, their fathers, their kings, their officials, everybody.

cards.question: What does Jeremiah say the LORD did with all that incense burned in Judah?
Jeremiah says the disaster came on them because they stopped serving the Queen of Heaven.

cards.text: Then one more word from the LORD. He repeats their own vow back to them, and says: 'Go ahead, then, do what you have promised! Keep your vows!' That's the 'fine, have it your way' nobody EVER wants to hear.

cards.question: The LORD swears by His great name. What will never again happen among the men of Judah living in Egypt?

answers.text: They will never invoke His name

cards.question: The LORD says He is watching over the men of Judah in Egypt. What is He watching over them for?

answers.text: For harm and not for good
For good and not for harm

cards.text: A few who escape the sword will return from Egypt to Judah. And then the whole remnant finds out who had it right all along.

cards.question: The whole remnant of Judah in Egypt will know whose ___ will stand: the LORD's or theirs.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives them a sign, so they'll know His threats will surely stand. And it's about Pharaoh Hophra, king of the very land they moved to.

cards.question: What does the LORD say will happen to Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt?

answers.text: He will be handed to his enemies
He will send Judah back home

cards.question: The LORD says Pharaoh Hophra will be handed over just as Zedekiah, king of Judah, was handed to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'The LORD of Hosts opens with...', 'Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, lying in ruins today.', 'No slideshow needed.' and 'They just LEFT it.' It is not the opening card, so the limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card runs six sentences: 'And God didn't spring this on anybody.', the sentence with the quote, the alarm clock line, 'Over.', 'And over.' and 'And OVER.'

findings.problem: The joke 'an alarm clock going off, and somebody hitting snooze. Over. And over. And OVER.' says the people ignored the warnings again and again. That gives away card 6, which asks whether the people turned from their wickedness when the prophets warned them (Jeremiah 44:5). The joke also tells verse 5 on a card that cites only 44:4.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: 'So the LORD says He has set His face...', 'And the remnant who decided to move to Egypt?', 'New zip code.' and 'Same God watching.'

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences. Only the passage's opening card (stop 1, card 1) may have up to three.

findings.problem: This card tells verse 15: 'the men who knew their wives were burning incense to other gods.' That gives away card 8, a true or false card about whether the women burned incense without their husbands knowing (Jeremiah 44:19). Card 8 needs a different question about verse 19, or no choice card there.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: 'Then they say what they WILL do.', the sentence about the vow, 'Wrong direction.' and 'Full commitment.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers are partly true elsewhere in the passage. In verse 18 the people say they have been 'perishing by sword and famine,' which matches 'Constant raids and little food'. In verse 13 the LORD says He punished Jerusalem by 'sword and famine and plague,' which overlaps 'Long years of drought and plague'. Each wrong answer is false only at this one moment.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: This story card only goes back over verse 18, which card 5 just asked about ('So their read is: life fell apart when we STOPPED'), and then adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. The credit card joke could ride on a card that tells new text.
The story card has three sentences: 'Then one more word from the LORD.', the sentence with the quote, and the 'fine, have it your way' line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 2, with six cards against four true or false and one fill in the blank. Both stops also use only one fill in the blank, so they share the same pattern.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
